A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MBQ and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material. Relocated sections and all six appendix case studies can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantization benchmarks, calibration ablations, GPU latency measurements and conversational error analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds rotation-based quantization comparisons and alternative reweighting experiments.

M1.justification: V2 introduces MBQ (Rot), combining modality balancing with rotation-based quantization in Section 4.3.3. The core channel-wise equalization objectives and fused kernel remain unchanged; the previously reported MBQ+GPTQ variant disappears with the W4A6 appendix results.

E1.justification: Both versions report the same calibration datasets, six vision-language benchmarks, MMLU and two conversational benchmarks. The new rotation and reweighting experiments reuse existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds an evaluated rotation-method comparison against QuaRot and SpinQuant in Table 5; these methods were only cited or discussed in v1. It also removes GPTQ versus MBQ+GPTQ comparisons under W4A6 for all six models. GPTQ remains evaluated in the main W3A16 tables despite disappearing from the baseline-description paragraph.

E3.justification: V2 removes the W4A6 evaluation configuration and introduces controls using randomly divided calibration-token groups and token-wise weighting. Retained experiments keep the stated 128 calibration examples, group size 128 and latency procedures. W3/W4 becoming W3A16/W4A16 clarifies notation; no protocol explanation accompanies the revised SEED scores.

E4.justification: Section 4.3.2 adds two controls testing random grouping and individual-token gradient weighting, reporting OCRBench accuracy 1.3 and 1.5 percentage points below MBQ, respectively. Existing calibration-dataset, MAE/MSE, encoder-quantization and language-only analyses remain, as do all six case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the reported accuracy comparisons. The added experiments continue point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: V2 revises small-model SEED scores and corresponding averages in the main and supplementary tables: LLaVA-onevision-7B MBQ W3/W3A16 changes from 66.4 to 69.7 on SEED and from 64.8 to 65.3 on average. It removes all W4A6 GPTQ/MBQ+GPTQ results and adds rotation comparisons and reweighting outcomes. The unexplained SEED revisions cannot establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the derivation: v1 uses a global average-gradient bound followed by approximate modality separation, whereas v2 explicitly decomposes the gradient-error product by modality and introduces successive inequalities in Equations 10–12. The resulting weighted MAE objective is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: differing modality sensitivities, gradient-balanced calibration and a fused three-bit kernel. The headline accuracy and speedup claims remain unchanged despite the revised result tables.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges limited gains over RTN and remaining FP16 performance gaps for large-model weight-activation quantization, motivating MBQ (Rot). It also explains the token-wise weighting control's poorer result through zero-gradient vision tokens whose quantization errors consequently receive no weight.

D1.justification: The disclosed calibration preparation, quantization granularity, kernel packing, RTX 4090 hardware, FlashAttention-2/QServe usage and code link remain unchanged. The rotation extension adds no corresponding implementation hyperparameters; relocated inference explanations and clarified precision labels do not change reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 adds FlatQuant and six references concerning sparse attention, decoding and efficient inference, broadening the introduction's context and positioning the rotation extension. The central distinction from modality-insensitive LLM quantization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The inference-process subsection moves to supplementary Section 6.1, and acceleration implementation becomes Method Section 3.3. V2 also condenses implementation prose, clarifies terminology and updates affiliations. Most existing narrative remains closely matched.

P2.justification: V1's main Table 2 is split into small- and large-model Tables 2–3; v2 adds rotation Table 5, removes W4A6 rows from the supplementary table and relocates Figure 2 to the appendix. Existing graphics and all six illustrated case studies are retained.

improvement.justification: The new controls and rotation comparisons add useful evidence, while the W4A6/GPTQ evidence is removed. V2 also introduces unexplained inconsistencies: v1's main and ablation tables agree on LLaVA-onevision-7B SEED scores of 71.1 for FP16 and 66.4 for MBQ; v2's main table reports 74.9 and 69.7 while its ablation table retains the old values. Added diagnostic value and reduced result consistency leave the net quality change uncertain.
